Irene — thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement looped me in with a couple of asks from legal before we can finalize the order form and signature. Attached is the version of your MSA/order form our counsel reviewed. Two items they flagged: 

1) Training carveouts — they want explicit language excluding patient/PHI data and anything marked as "Customer Confidential" from any model training or long-term telemetry use.
2) Output ownership — they need confirmation that any customer-supplied materials (images/reports) will not be used to retrain models or otherwise generate derivatives for third-party reuse.

We can share the redline but wanted your read on whether Redwood is open to a narrow carveout + telemetry aggregation clause. Our target: sign by end of month (5/31).

- The carveout needs to explicitly call out "customer-submitted medical images, diagnostic reports, and any PHI as defined under HIPAA". This is non-negotiable for us.
- For telemetry/feedback, counsel suggested "aggregated, de-identified usage telemetry for performance and safety monitoring only" — that sounds reasonable to them if spelled out.

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 13:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on IP & training language in MSA + Order Form

Sam — thanks for the specificity, that helps. Commercial note: the carveout itself doesn’t force Dedicated/Private — NeoHealth can choose Hosted with the carveout in the MSA; however, we should flag that some advanced features (model fine-tuning, persistent embeddings for cross-account search) are not compatible with an account-level training opt-out. If NeoHealth wants those features, we can discuss a Private deployment option.

Suggested compromise language (draft snippet for Laura to adapt):
"Customer Data" shall not be used to train, fine-tune, or otherwise materially update Redwood Inference models for general availability. Notwithstanding the foregoing, Redwood may use aggregated, de-identified telemetry and model performance metrics for the sole purpose of internal safety and quality improvements, provided such data cannot be re-associated with Customer or individual persons. Customer may elect to mark specific datasets as "Excluded from Model Improvements," in which case Redwood will treat such datasets as exempt from training or retention for model tuning purposes.

If that sounds workable, Laura can produce a tracked-change version to finalize. We can also provide an ops playbook describing how excluded assets are tagged and purged during log retention windows.

—Ben
Ben Carter | Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Inline: suggested snippet included above]

Sam/Irene/Ben — thanks. I’ve taken Ben’s commercial snippet and produced a tracked-changes redline for the MSA and a narrow Order Form appendix that enumerates the carveouts and the operational controls (tagging, retention, audit evidence). High-level summary of edits: 

1) Training & Retrain Use: added explicit exclusion for "Customer-Provided PHI and customer-marked excluded materials"; added a process clause for how to mark and purge data; added a 30-day SLA for acknowledgement of requests to mark data excluded.
2) Output Ownership: clarified that customer retains ownership of their uploaded content and any direct outputs created from that content; Redwood expressly reserves rights to aggregated non-identifiable derivatives used only for service quality.
3) Feedback License: narrowed to telemetry/aggregated metrics only; removed any broad perpetual license language.

I attach two documents: msaredline_v3.docx (tracked changes) and orderform_narrow_use.pdf (appendix that NeoHealth can sign). If NeoHealth accepts, we can move to signature via DocuSign and include a short Ops attachment describing tagging/retention.

Next steps: 
- Sam: confirm the 30-day acknowledgement SLA is acceptable to NeoHealth legal.
- Irene: confirm NeoHealth product/ops have what they need to operationalize the tag/purge flow.

If all good, I’ll route to Contracts for final sign-off.

Regards,
Laura Bennett | Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
